cards.canonical_statement: For every natural order n and every derivative domain uIcc(a,b), evaluating the Taylor polynomial centered at c at c itself gives f(c), without smoothness assumptions.
cards.proof_strategy: Write the finite Taylor expansion at its center.
sketch_steps: Write the finite Taylor expansion at its center.
All positive-degree factors (c-c)^k vanish.
The zero-degree coefficient is the original function value.
Thus only f(c) remains, including at order n=0.

cards.proof_strategy: Use a≤b to identify the unordered derivative domain with [a,b].
sketch_steps: Use a≤b to identify the unordered derivative domain with [a,b].
Retain C^(n+1) regularity and the uniform derivative bound on the entire interval.
Apply the normed Taylor mean-remainder estimate at x.
Replace real norms by absolute values and preserve its n! denominator, including n=0 and a=b.

cards.canonical_statement: For every natural n and b>0, the degree-n Taylor polynomial of x^(n+1) centered at zero with derivative domain [0,b] evaluates to zero at b, while b^(n+1)>0. Finite Taylor truncations need not equal the function.
cards.proof_strategy: Expand the degree-n Taylor polynomial as the sum of coefficients of orders k≤n.
sketch_steps: Expand the degree-n Taylor polynomial as the sum of coefficients of orders k≤n.
The k-th within derivative of x^(n+1) is a falling-factorial coefficient times x^(n+1-k).
Every exponent n+1-k is positive, so each coefficient at zero vanishes.
The Taylor value is zero while positivity of b gives a strictly positive actual function value, for every n including zero.

by
  constructor
  · rw [taylor_within_apply]
    apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
    intro k hk
    have hk' : k ≤ n := Nat.le_of_lt_succ (Finset.mem_range.mp hk)
    rw [Set.uIcc_of_le hb.le, iteratedDerivWithin_pow (show (0:ℝ) ∈ Set.Icc 0 b from ⟨le_rfl, hb.le⟩) (uniqueDiffOn_Icc hb) (n+1) k]
    have hn : n+1-k ≠ 0 := by omega
    simp [zero_pow hn]
  · exact pow_pos hb _

cards.canonical_statement: For every nonzero real c, the terms c/n tend to zero as n→∞, yet the real series Σ c/n is not summable. The totalized n=0 term has no effect on either claim.
cards.proof_strategy: Use the natural reciprocal limit to show c/n tends to zero.
sketch_steps: Use the natural reciprocal limit to show c/n tends to zero.
Rewrite division as c times n inverse.
A nonzero constant multiplier preserves and reflects summability.
Summability would contradict divergence of the harmonic series, proving the term-zero condition is insufficient.

cards.canonical_statement: If 0≤q<1 and |u(n)|≤c*q^n for every n, then u is summable and every n-term partial sum differs from its total sum by at most c*q^n/(1-q).
cards.proof_strategy: The geometric majorant with ratio q is summable.
sketch_steps: The geometric majorant with ratio q is summable.
Absolute comparison implies summability of u.
Its finite initial sums therefore converge to its total sum.
Bound successive partial-sum distances by c*q^n and sum the geometric tail.
This yields the stated certified error bound for every truncation length, including zero.

cards.canonical_statement: If the ordered natural partial sums of Σ u(n)*a^n converge to c and |b|<|a|, then Σ u(n)*b^n is unconditionally summable. The boundary series is allowed to converge only conditionally.
cards.proof_strategy: Turn convergence of the ordered boundary partial sums into the Cauchy property.
sketch_steps: Turn convergence of the ordered boundary partial sums into the Cauchy property.
This bounds the boundary terms u(n)*a^n.
Strictly smaller |b| gives geometric decay with ratio |b|/|a|<1.
Apply the power-series interior convergence theorem to obtain absolute, hence unconditional, summability at b.

cards.proof_strategy: The exact summability criterion for a real geometric series is |q|<1.

Assume summability for a ratio with |q|≥1.
The criterion would imply the contradictory strict inequality.
Conclude nonsummability for the entire boundary-and-exterior family.

cards.proof_strategy: The strict condition |q|<1 provides an open neighborhood on which the geometric series converges.

Transfer the derivative across the neighborhood equality; no unproved general interchange of infinite sums and derivatives is assumed.

cards.lean_target: example (q : ℝ) (hq : |q| < 1) : HasDerivAt (fun x : ℝ => ∑' n : ℕ, x^n) (1/(1-q)^2) q
cards.lean_witness:
by
  have hn : (1:ℝ)-q ≠ 0 := by have := (abs_lt.mp hq).2; linarith
  have hd := (hasDerivAt_const q (1:ℝ)).div ((hasDerivAt_const q (1:ℝ)).sub (hasDerivAt_id q)) hn
  have hd' : HasDerivAt (fun x : ℝ => 1/(1-x)) (1/(1-q)^2) q := by convert! hd using 1 <;> simp
  apply hd'.congr_of_eventuallyEq
  filter_upwards [(isOpen_lt continuous_abs continuous_const).mem_nhds hq] with x hx
  simpa only [one_div] using tsum_geometric_of_norm_lt_one (show ‖x‖ < 1 from hx)
